title: Constant sheaves are acyclic on irreducible Noetherian spaces
statement: Let X be an irreducible Noetherian topological space (meaning every nonempty set of closed subsets has a minimal element for inclusion), and let A be an abelian group. On the site of open subsets of X with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let A_X be the constant abelian sheaf, namely the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value A [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then H^q(X,A_X)=0 for every integer q>0 [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology].

proof.text: For every nonempty open U of X, U is irreducible: two nonempty opens of U are nonempty opens of X and therefore meet. The constant-sheaf section calculation and restriction compatibility are exactly [lem-sc-irreducible-constant-sections]. For the empty open, the sheaf axiom gives the zero group. Thus every restriction map of A_X between opens is surjective, so A_X is flasque in the sense of [def-sc-zariski-flasque].

source.place: Lemma 02UW proof: constant sheaf on an irreducible Noetherian space is flasque

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-topological-flasque-acyclic] to the flasque sheaf A_X. It gives H^q(X,A_X)=0 for every q>0.
